articles.title: Chemicals, Covid and cabbage: why 2026 has been an amazing year for documentaries
articles.summary: With Musk, NAZA and You Can See Everything finding large audiences, non-fiction cinema is poised to break through. But there are plenty more gripping stories waiting for their turn in the spotlight There comes a time in the life of every film enthusiast when they must set aside foolish fictions and face up to some hard truths. Specifically, that time arrives each November in the form of the International Documentary Film Festival Amsterdam (IDFA for short), with its tales of crisis and strife, angry resistance and everyday human kindness. The world’s largest documentary festival plays out in the city’s twinkling downtown district, quite near the torture museum, and provides a sharp corrective to the confected dramas and A-list pageantry of Cannes, Toronto and Venice. articles.title: Blade Runner 2099: fans will have no idea what is happening in this sci-fi sequel. Why is it even on TV?
articles.summary: If you’re a cyberpunk who loves ennui and watching actors you can’t see speak words you can’t hear, get stuck in! The rest of us will just be baffled and bored Why is James Bond not a TV series by now? Harry Potter, Lord of the Rings, Alien, Star Wars – all given the TV treatment. Franchise-mining is fantastic business, maximising attention share in order to sell adverts. So why not Bond, which is co-owned by Amazon? Maybe watching a punchy sex addict every week, saying his name with weirdly administrative syntax, might just be … too much? I entertained these thoughts while struggling to get through another series expansion: Blade Runner 2099 (Prime Video, from Wednesday). I’m a fan of the films. articles.summary: As he invests in 60,0000 sq ft of midwest real estate, the celebrated artist explains bringing ‘independent thinking’ back to fine china “The worth of hand-painted china depends mainly upon the hand ,” reads an advertisement dating from 1910 and displayed just inside the entrance of the Pickard China factory, a sprawling, 60,000 sq ft brick building just outside of Chicago. “Most of the large staff of artists at the Pickard studios have been trained in the great art centers of Europe, and each piece of Pickard is painted from start to finish by the same master craftsman.” Those statements are a distant echo from another age. articles.title: ‘Reminds me of home’: why Coming to America is my feelgood movie
articles.summary: The latest in our series of writers picking their most rewatched comfort films is an ode to Eddie Murphy’s beloved culture-clash comedy “Good morning, my neighbors!” A young Eddie Murphy shouts from the balcony of a shady apartment building. In the bustling Queens neighborhood, he sticks out like a sore thumb with his foreign accent, tailored blazing jacket and red tie. “Hey, fuck you!” A voice yells from below and Murphy repeats the phrase, believing that it’s a greeting rather than an insult. It’s one of the standout scenes from the film Coming to America, because it’s so absurd but effective in that there is a cultural clash going on here.
